report:
Clinical failure: small-study effects (odds ratio)

Comparison: Intervention / Control

Methods

Statistical analyses were performed using RC MetaStudio (version 0.6.0; Research Consultancy) [1] with the R packages metafor (version 5.2.1) [2] and meta (version 8.5-0) [3]. Small-study effects procedures run: Harbord test; Rücker AS+RE test; Peters test; Ordinary funnel plot [4, 5, 6, 7, 8].

Results

Primary asymmetry test: Harbord test
Result: P = 0.698
Usable studies: 7
Bias coefficient: −0.5687 (SE 1.385)

Funnel plot asymmetry can reflect publication bias, heterogeneity, study design, or chance.

Interpret the plots and tests together. No single result proves or rules out publication bias.

Data and eligibility:

Effect measure: Odds ratio (OR)

Studies analyzed: 7

Confidence level: 95% confidence interval

Primary test: Harbord test

Observed standard-error range: [0.27755775, 1.5672852]

Heterogeneity (τ², REML): 0.2893

Continuity correction: Studies with any zero cell

Tests:

Harbord test (primary)

  Studies: 7

  Result: P = 0.698.

  Test statistic: −0.4107

  Coefficient: −0.5687 (SE 1.385)

  Model: Harbord native metabin model



Rücker AS+RE test (exploratory)

  Studies: 7

  Result: P = 0.501.

  Test statistic: −0.7253

  Coefficient: −1.503 (SE 2.072)

  Model: Rücker AS+RE (ASD + Thompson)



Peters test (exploratory)

  Studies: 7

  Result: P = 0.871.

  Test statistic: −0.1714

  Coefficient: −9.901 (SE 57.77)

  Model: Peters native metabin model

Pooled comparison:

Common effect

  Estimate: 0.6222

  95% confidence interval: 0.4299 to 0.9006



Random effects (REML)

  Estimate: 0.6379

  95% confidence interval: 0.3439 to 1.183



These are model comparisons, not estimates corrected for publication bias.

Method details:

Harbord test

  Package: meta 8.5-0

  Predictor: Harbord Z/V on 1/sqrt(V), where V is the native score variance

  Weighting: native Harbord score variance V

  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test

  Degrees of freedom: 5.000

  Exact p-value: 0.698272

  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='OR', incr=0.5, method.incr='only0', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.OR.model, method.bias='Harbord', k.min=7, level=0.95)



Rücker AS+RE test

  Package: meta 8.5-0

  Predictor: ASD effect on native ASD standard error

  Weighting: native AS+RE additive REML weights

  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test

  Degrees of freedom: 5.000

  Exact p-value: 0.50080289

  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='ASD', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); meta::metabias(x=prepared.ASD.model, method.bias='Thompson', k.min=7, level=0.95)



Peters test

  Package: meta 8.5-0

  Predictor: 1/(n.e+n.c), with native Peters seTE=sqrt(1/(event.e+event.c)+1/(non-events.e+non-events.c))

  Weighting: 1/Peters seTE^2

  Inference: t-based meta::metabias test

  Degrees of freedom: 5.000

  Exact p-value: 0.87064631

  Call: meta::metabin(event.e, n.e, event.c, n.c, sm='OR', incr=0.5, method.incr='only0', common=TRUE, random=TRUE, method.tau='REML', level=0.95); prepared.OR.model$TE <- prepared.effects; prepared.OR.model$seTE <- prepared.standard.errors; meta::metabias(x=prepared.OR.model, method.bias='Peters', k.min=7, level=0.95)

Methods not applicable:

No additional methods were marked not applicable.

References

1. Salman, A., Fatima, K., Khan, M. S., Siddiqi, T. J., & Usman, M. S. (2026). RC MetaStudio: open-source desktop software for meta-analysis (Version 0.6.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23118556

5. Rücker, G., Schwarzer, G., & Carpenter, J. R. (2008). Arcsine test for publication bias in meta-analyses with binary outcomes. Statistics in Medicine, 27(5), 746-763. doi:10.1002/sim.2971.

6. Thompson, S. G., & Sharp, S. J. (1999). Explaining heterogeneity in meta-analysis: A comparison of methods. Statistics in Medicine, 18(20), 2693-2708.

7. Peters, J. L., Sutton, A. J., Jones, D. R., Abrams, K. R., & Rushton, L. (2006). Comparison of two methods to detect publication bias in meta-analysis. JAMA, 295(6), 676-680. doi:10.1001/jama.295.6.676.

report:
Clinical failure: random-effects meta-analysis (odds ratio)

Comparison: Intervention / Control

Methods

Statistical analyses were performed using RC MetaStudio (version 0.6.0; Research Consultancy) [1] with the R package metafor (version 5.2.1) [2]. Odds ratios were pooled using a random-effects model with the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator of between-study variance. Confidence intervals (95%) used the normal approximation. Heterogeneity was assessed with Cochran’s Q and I².

Results

In total, 1 study was included (27 participants in Intervention, 27 in Control); 18 studies were excluded. The pooled odds ratio was 0.57 (95% CI 0.17 to 1.92; z = −0.91; P = 0.365). Heterogeneity: not estimable (k = 1).
